ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a square ABCD, with A at the lower left, B at the lower right, C at the upper right, and D at the upper left. P is at the midpoint of the left side DA, Q is at the midpoint of the right side BC, and R is at the midpoint of the upper side CD. The figure draws AR and BR, forming the large triangle ARB, and also draws AQ and BP, which intersect at point O. The shaded part is inside triangle ARB, but does not include the unshaded bottom triangle AOB. Reasoning: Let the side length of the square be 1, and take coordinates A=(0,0), B=(1,0), C=(1,1), D=(0,1). Because P, Q, and R are respectively the midpoints of sides DA, BC, and CD, P=(0,1/2), Q=(1,1/2), R=(1/2,1). Line AQ passes through (0,0) and (1,1/2), with equation y=x/2. Line BP passes through (1,0) and (0,1/2), with equation y=(1-x)/2. Equating the two expressions gives x/2=(1-x)/2, so x=1/2, y=1/4, therefore O=(1/2,1/4). Triangle ARB has base AB of length 1 and height 1, so its area is 1/2. Triangle AOB has base AB of length 1 and height 1/4, so its area is (1/2)(1)(1/4)=1/8. Shaded area = area of triangle ARB - area of triangle AOB = 1/2 - 1/8 = 3/8.

method.method_draft: Use a coordinate/area subtraction setup. From the image, note that the hatched region lies inside triangle ARB, except for the unshaded bottom triangle AOB, where O is the intersection of the drawn segments AQ and BP. From the text, take ABCD as a square, with P and Q midpoints of the left and right sides and R the midpoint of the top side. Assign coordinates A=(0,0), B=(1,0), C=(1,1), D=(0,1), so P=(0,1/2), Q=(1,1/2), R=(1/2,1). Line AQ has equation y=x/2, and line BP has equation y=(1-x)/2, so they meet at O=(1/2,1/4). Then area triangle ARB is 1/2 of the square, and area triangle AOB is (1/2)(1)(1/4)=1/8 of the square. Therefore shaded fraction = 1/2 - 1/8 = 3/8.
